answer: A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The fable multiplier is published, charged in terrace, and nectar lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1281 identities would post 2542 proofs and burn roughly 87 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
